info.title: Invinite API
info.description:
Invinite financial data API. Each operation has a base credit cost: `x-credits` is the base cost; responses add 1 credit per started 1,000 rows beyond the first 1,000; `X-Credits-Charged` reports the final debit and `X-Credits-Remaining` what is left of the plan's included credits after it. A `304 Not Modified` costs nothing. `GET /v1/me/usage` returns your account's usage by day, product family and key (it costs no credits).

**Coverage.** Financial data covers US SEC registrants and their US listings; a symbol that is not a US SEC registrant (or a crypto pair such as `X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404. A known company with no data in a family (for example no statements yet) answers 404 with `code: not_covered`; an empty page of a covered company stays 200 with an empty list. `GET /v1/companies` lists every known company.

## Webhooks

Alerts (`POST /v1/alerts`) deliver their events to your destinations (`POST /v1/destinations`) as [Standard Webhooks](https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks/blob/main/spec/standard-webhooks.md): `alert.fired`, `alert.fired.batch`, `alert.status_changed`, `destination.disabled`, `destination.test`, `account.fire_cap_reached`, `alert_user.fire_cap_reached`; see `x-webhooks` for each `data` object. Every event is also on the pull feed `GET /v1/alert-events`.

Every delivery is a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`, the body `{type, timestamp, data}` (or the destination's `body_template`) and the headers `webhook-id` (the event id; a batch: its `bat_…` id), `webhook-timestamp` (unix seconds) and `webhook-signature`: space-separated `v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256 of <webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<raw body>>`, keyed with the base64-DECODED bytes of the destination's `whsec_…` secret — any Standard Webhooks library verifies it. After `POST /v1/destinations/{id}:rotate-secret` the old secret keeps signing beside the new one for 24 h (two `v1` entries). Reject a timestamp older than 5 minutes. Any 2xx within 10 s acknowledges; redirects are not followed; a body above 256 KB is not sent. A failed attempt is retried after [0, 5 s, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 5 h, 10 h, 10 h, 10 h, 34 h] (attempt n waits the n-th step) plus up to 10 % jitter; the delivery is dead after attempt 10. A 410 disables the destination at once; so do 72 h of nothing but failures with at least 10 failed attempts in a row (a `destination.disabled` event on the feed and a mail; `PATCH` with `status: active` re-enables it). Delivery is at-least-once and unordered: dedupe on `webhook-id`, order by `timestamp`. A `batch_webhook` destination receives `alert.fired.batch` with the pending events in `data.events[]` (dedupe on each `data.event_id`).

Fires and deliveries cost no credits; no daily fire cap; at most 60 fires per alert per rolling hour (beyond: suppressed and counted in the next fire's `suppressed_since_last`); an Enterprise contract may set a daily cap (beyond it: written to the feed with `delivery_skipped: fire_cap`, not delivered; one `account.fire_cap_reached` per day). An end user's `max_fires_per_day` (or the account default) caps that user first: beyond it `delivery_skipped: alert_user_fire_cap`, not counted against the account's cap, one `alert_user.fire_cap_reached` per user and day.

## Licensing

| Tier | display | redistribute | rag | train | audio | redistribute_api | resell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FREE | – | – | – | – | – | – | – |
| LITE | – | – | – | – | – | – | – |
| STANDARD | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – | – | – | – |
| PRO | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – | ✓ | – | – |
| ENTERPRISE | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓* | ✓ | ✓* | – |

\* Depending on the contract.

Invinite data may be used inside the licensee's own organisation from LITE and, from STANDARD, shown and redistributed inside the licensee's own product (on screen, in exports and in embedded widgets) with attribution ("Source: Invinite"). Passing the data on through the licensee's own API is an ENTERPRISE right, granted in the contract. It may never be resold, relicensed, white-labelled or offered as a data feed as the licensee's own data, at any tier, under any contract.

Internal use: Every paid plan may use the data inside the licensee's own organisation: analysis, internal tools and dashboards for the licensee's own staff. Nothing is shown or passed to third parties below STANDARD.

Policy version: 2026-11-draft-2. Draft — pending counsel sign-off.

Audio files carry a forensic watermark that identifies the recording. Audio is subject to per-company takedown and may not be re-hosted.

SEC data: Figures and filings originate from SEC EDGAR; the standardisation, mapping and derived metrics are Invinite's.

News: News text is Invinite's own summary of the issuer's or the SEC's publication (the publisher's text and media are never served); the licensee shows the attribution (publisher, source URL and date) next to it; the resale rule applies.

PDF documents: Branded PDFs of transcripts and news items are permanent URLs to one shared file per version. They may be shown, downloaded and forwarded unmodified with the notice page intact; the resale rule applies unchanged. News PDFs carry Invinite's summary of the issuer's or the SEC's publication under the attribution stated on their notice page; a PDF disappears when the item is taken down or its source's reuse is denied.

Every `/v1/*` data operation carries `x-license`, the minimum use right its data ships with; `GET /status/licensing` serves the same matrix per route, rendered at [data.invinite.com/docs/licensing](https://data.invinite.com/docs/licensing). `/v1/me` and `/v1/me/usage` serve no licensed data and carry none.

## Status

[`/status`](/status) reports product-family uptime in `services` and request health and latency by documentation group in `groups`. Windows with too few requests have no figures. [`/status/licensing`](/status/licensing) serves the licensing matrix per route. The status routes need no API key and are cached for 5 minutes. The public status page is [status.data.invinite.com](https://status.data.invinite.com): a snapshot of `/status` every 15 minutes plus an external reachability probe of the API.

Uptime is the share of requests answered without a server error, measured by the API per product family; a window with too little traffic to judge shows no figure. Status reflects the last 24 hours.

Product families: Company, Financials, SEC Filings, Insider Trades, Institutional Ownership, Ownership Filings, IPOs, Market, Metadata, Earnings Calls, News, WebSocket, Account, Alerts, Bulk Data.

Measured documentation groups: Corporate actions, Calendar, Instruments, Companies, Funds, Catalog, Macro, News, Financials, Metrics, Offerings, Holders, Insider trades, Ownership, Filings, Bulk data, Events, Call analytics, Transcripts, Guidance, Investor documents, Alerts, Alert users, Alert events, Destinations, Scripts.

AlertCondition.title: AlertCondition
AlertCondition.description: What the alert watches; the fields depend on `type` (each field names the types that take it; any other field is refused). Companies: `ciks` / `symbols` (at most 100 in all) or, for single-company types, `cik` / `symbol`. A symbol is resolved to its CIK at create. Price types (`price`, `price_move`, `volume_spike`, `price_reminder`) and `script` watch ONE instrument: `symbol` + `asset_class`. A `script` alert runs a script version (`/v1/scripts`) at each close of `interval`; alerts with the same version, instrument, interval, inputs and frequency share one evaluation. An `indicator` alert takes a built-in `template` (`GET /v1/alert-templates`) or a structured `condition` (+ optional `filters`) on `symbol` / `interval`; alerts crossing a constant on the same indicator, instrument and interval share one evaluation whatever the threshold. Coverage: `filing_keyword`, `fundamental_metric` and `earnings_results` work only for companies whose filings and financials Invinite processes (any other company answers 404 `not_covered`); `earnings_call_keyword` takes any company with captured calls. US ETFs: `dividend`, `event_countdown` (`ex_dividend` / `dividend_payment`), `filing` and `filing_keyword` take an ETF ticker (SPY or a trust series such as TQQQ; a series ETF is stored by symbol and fires only on events that name it, never on another series' filing of its trust); `earnings_call`, `earnings_call_keyword`, `earnings_results`, `fundamental_metric`, `news`, `news_keyword` and an `earnings_call` countdown refuse an ETF of either identity (its ticker or a fund registrant's CIK) by name (400 `invalid_parameter`).
